## Design

### 2026-10-11 – October 8: 5tarbie Design!!

**4h**

October 8: 5tarbie Design!!

Starting off my first ever PCB project with some rough edges.

After setting up the components for the starbie, what do each of the symbols mean, and how do they work?

![Screenshot 2026-10-08 183333](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/UMx8GtS67VH17jO55ZdjXA5Q5GgA51Ts/8b7c770624b422ba9c197613c7c519e49124876cdf99bd99bc0d590864620784.png)

In short, this is how they work:

- The microcontroller essentially acts like the "brain"
- The buttons to create a functioning base
- The OLED is the displayer for a specific response
- The Conn 01 by 08 is the sensor
- The "box" is the environmental sensor
- GND stands for ground
- +3.3V stands for power, V probably stands for Volts
- SCL stands for a clock signal to establish communication
- SDA stands for the data that carries info to the microcontroller
- R is a resistor that limits an electrical current

During the schematic editing, I wondered why the components didn't look exactly like the reference image, so then I realized I had to manually add the components above using the P and L buttons. I also couldn't figure out how to connect the wires, but simply pressing W and connecting both points does the trick:

![Screenshot 2026-10-8 095457](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/UMx8GtS67VH17jO55ZdjXA5Q5GgA51Ts/44110102ebfb132df31f26e130433adf0ee1d7e4591bb187fbda4131b0c0f6cf.png)

When working on the footprint assignment, I realized J1 had over 10000 results!, i then realized I had a search bar to narrow it down and I got the file assignments in, though I don't know why my version doesn't really match with the reference image. For example, U1  has XIAO and U2 has DHT11, and the image shows the exact opposite! After searching, I can't really force them to switch, yet I don't have any errors after following the guide.

Woah! The PCB editor looks like space, and for some reason, my design is somewhat accurate to the image, but the parts still look the same, so moving on:

![Screenshot 2026-10-08 214006](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/UMx8GtS67VH17jO55ZdjXA5Q5GgA51Ts/3177112e5e6537ae676a7ed57e52b9519031e35bb6833649b33249ceb2d1de42.png)

I then realized that I hadn't read that the components needed to be connected by the F.Cu lines from the guided blue lines (B.Cu?). I also noticed that the "wires" can't intersect unless they are part of the same connecting system.

![Screenshot 2026-10-08 183053](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/UMx8GtS67VH17jO55ZdjXA5Q5GgA51Ts/db7c66bcd9fe5d4a70535557d98d85b75ae5d36919a1e1fb75dfb8ce24e3882b.png)

October 9: 5tarbie Design!!

Okay, so my mind is clearer, and the instructions are starting to become easier. However, the first thing I run into is the pain-stakingly  amount of errors I had in my DRC (Design Rules Checker). Easy problems with the border, I finished the overlapping marks and the entire star lit up a bit.
